name: Tempester n°6: SysEx import over USB protected from DIN messages
explanation: The SysEx state (SRAM ring 0x3C000, counter [address], command [address], sub-state [address]) is shared by USB and DIN. The DIN parser [routine] called [routine] (reset of this state) on every DIN status byte 0x80-0xF7, and [routine] (end of SysEx) on every DIN F7, without looking at the setting « MIDI: Sysex IN+OUT Cable » ([address]). A single DIN note during a USB import therefore erased the transfer; at the F7, [routine] gave up without telling the screen, which stayed on « Receiving … » (forum: bug 18 by Roger_Linn, smak). The other way round, every end of a USB SysEx cleared the DIN running status ([routine]). The three calls are diverted to routines that keep the original behaviour when the SysEx cable is DIN ([address] == 1) and isolate the two ports otherwise. Left outside the patch: the [address] = 0 written by [routine] (at most one DIN note lost per USB SysEx command). Code added at 0x9D07B000-0x9D07B083.

edits.why: jal 0x9d07b000 ; DIN parser, status byte 0x80-0xF7: jal [address] (unconditional SysEx reset) -> routine A, which does it only if the SysEx cable is DIN
jal 0x9d07b030 ; DIN parser, F7: jal [address] (end of SysEx) -> routine B, which does it only if the SysEx cable is DIN
jal 0x9d07b060 ; [routine]: jal [address] (DIN parser state) -> routine C, which resets it only if the SysEx cable is DIN
lui t0,0xa001 ; A: reads [address] (SysEx cable: 0 none, 1 DIN, 2 USB)
j [address] ; A: DIN cable -> original full reset (tail jump, returns to [address])
j [address] ; A: otherwise -> only the DIN parser state (running status, data pointer)
j [address] ; B: DIN cable -> original end of SysEx
jr ra ; B: otherwise -> DIN F7 ignored
lui t0,0xa001 ; C: reads [address] (ra already saved by [routine] at 0x10(sp))
j [address] ; C: DIN cable -> DIN state reset as originally
jr ra ; C: otherwise -> the DIN parser state is not touched
